30. COMMITMENTS AND CONTINGENCIES
(a) Contingent Liabilities
Guarantees and bonds

Commitments given include primarily customs bonds. The bonds are held in the ordinary course of business. No losses are
anticipated in respect of these contingent liabilities.
Commitments received include primarily customer guarantees.
Commitments received/given are all held with local banks.
(b) Contingent Liabilities
Legal claims
a) In 1999, a supplier launched a claim of Kshs 44,100,000 for damages relating to termination of transporter agreement.
b) In 2009, a distributor filled a claim of Kshs 75,950,163 against the company for refund for product allegedly paid
and never supplied, loss of income and damages for alleged assault during station take-over.
Based on legal advice received from the company’s lawyer, the directors are of the opinion that the liabilities will not
materialize.
Contingent liability relating to parent company
An amount of Kshs 196 million (USD 2,427,388) (2009: Kshs 189 million (USD 2,427,388) exists as at 31 December 2010 for an
unsettled invoice to the parent company, Total Outremer, and has not been provided for in the Total Kenya Limited’s books
as the goods were not received by Total Kenya Limited. Management is keenly following up on the matter and is of the view
that the ultimate resolution of this matter will not have any impact on the company’s financial position or liquidity.
